landing.sloCheckCompDatastoresExpectedBounds: SLOs are used to check whether our components and data-stores are operating within expected bounds.
landing.inspectSLObreakingViolating: Inspect which SLOs we are breaking/violating.
landing.statisticsWholeMonitorUnit: Statistics across the whole monitoring unit, i.e. all units and shared components.
landing.gatherInsightsVarUnitsProblems: Gather insights how the various units are performing and identify which unit is having problems.
landing.allowsUnitLevelStability: Allows unit-level insights, e.g. infrastructure and application monitoring stability.
landing.agentDesc: Learn which unit has agents that are experiencing problems.
landing.acceptorDesc: Agents transmit data to acceptors. Acceptors are therefore the first-mile for most of the data transmitted to Instana.
landing.serverlessAcceptorDesc: Serverless-acceptors are the first-mile for serverless tracing and monitoring, when data is transmitted directly from a serverless enitity to our back end, without an Instana agent in between.
landing.cashiersDesc: Cashier components are used for generating usage stats for customers and internal accounting.
landing.applMonitorDesc: Dashboards showing how application data, i.e. traces and spans, are written and read.
landing.syntheticsMonitorDesc: Dashboards showing how Synthetic data are written and read.
landing.syntheticsAcceptorDesc: The synthetics-acceptor is the receiver for the Synthetic data transmitted to Instana.
landing.syntheticsHealthProcessorDesc: The synthetics-health-processor executes health rules for the Synthetic data transmitted to Instana.
landing.syntheticsMonitorWriterDesc: The synthetics-writer ingests synthetic test result data into ClickHouse.
landing.syntheticsMonitorReaderDesc: The synthetics-reader queries data from ClickHouse, Groundskeeper, and External Storage.
landing.infrastructureMetricsDesc: Information about our infrastructure metric pipeline.
landing.endUserMonitoringDesc: Information about our website monitoring processing pipeline. This includes acceptance of end-user requests as well as processing and writing of the received beacons.
landing.overviewDesc: Gain an overview across the whole EUM pipeline. This dashboard is a combination and subset of the eum-acceptor, eum-processor and appdata-writer dashboards.
landing.landingEumAcceptorDesc: eum-acceptor accepts end-user requests, validates, maps and transmits them via Kafka for processing.
landing.jsStackTraceTranslatorDesc: xParses and attempts to make JavaScript stack traces more readable by means of JavaScript source maps.xx
landing.eumProcessorDesc: eum-processor enriches received beacons and forwards them to Kafka for persistence.
landing.eumHealthHrocessorDesc: eum-health-processor reads processed beacons from Kafka and executes rules on buckets of beacons.
landing.appdataWriterDesc: appdata-writer persists enriched beacons to ClickHouse.
landing.errorSimulatorDesc: Trigger JavaScript errors to verify website monitoring behavior.
landing.internalMonitoringUnitInstanaEmail: Did you know that these features are also available on customer tenant units? They are hidden by                    default, but can be shown with a small trick. To enable them click 10 times (within 2 seconds) on                    the non-interactive part of our main navigation!
landing.entityStatisticsDesc: Shows how many infrastructure entities are monitored within this unit, broken down by plugin.
landing.entityAndMetricStatisticsDesc: Shows how many infrastructure entities and metrics are monitored within this unit, broken down by plugin.
landing.agentsDesc: Metrics for all agents reporting to this unit.
landing.graphExplorerDesc: Use this to analyze graph relations between infrastructure entities existing within this unit.
landing.infrastructureEntityVerDesc: Inspect versions for a single infrastructure entity and visualize when they were created and for how long they were valid/
landing.internalEventsDesc: Request a list of internal events such as Agent Crash Reports
landing.saaSMonitoringUnitsDesc: These units exist to monitor our own SaaS installations. They themselves are SaaS units.
landing.unitMonitoringGreenDesc: Unit monitoring the Green (GCP) SaaS installation.
landing.unitMonitoringOrangeDesc: Unit monitoring the Orange (GCP) SaaS installation.
landing.unitMonitoringCoralDesc: Unit monitoring the Coral (GCP) SaaS installation.
landing.unitMonitoringRedDesc: Unit monitoring the Red (AWS US) SaaS installation.
landing.unitMonitoringBlueDesc: Unit monitoring the Blue (AWS EU) SaaS installation.
landing.internalDesc: A SaaS unit monitoring the internal development units.
landing.devUnitsDesc: These units are designed to be used mainly by the product organization of Instana to continue to evolve Instana itself.
landing.testDesc: Auto-deployed from the develop branches every hour.
landing.nightlyDesc: Auto-deployed from the develop branches every night.
landing.stagingDesc: Auto-deployed from the release-XYZ branch on every commit.
landing.previewDesc: Manually deployed latest release-XYZ branch 1 week before the SaaS release. Sales / CS / SE / PM has access to this unit.
landing.releaseDesc: Manually deployed latest release-XYZ on demand.
landing.demoUnitsDesc: These units are frequently used by the whole company for demo / presentation purposes.
landing.demousDescUs: A SaaS demo unit running within the US.
landing.demousDescEu: A SaaS demo unit running within the EU.
landing.eumDescription: Metrics for end-user monitoring components within this unit.
landing.logMonitoringDesc: Information about our log processing pipeline.

kafka.suspensionChartExplanation: Suspension is an indication of how much application execution might have been delayed by the JVM, OS or CPU during the last second. This is predominantly caused by GC activations.

metaElastic.suspensionChartExplanation: Suspension is an indication of how much application execution might have been delayed by the JVM, OS or CPU during the last second. This is predominantly caused by GC activations.

appDataStatistic.spanDropSumChartExplanation_1: Shows whether spans are being dropped and why:
appDataStatistic.spanDropSumChartExplanation_2: Processed: how many spans got successfully processed.
appDataStatistic.spanDropSumChartExplanation_3: Dropped due to global throttler: dropped due a global rate limiter (config.hard.spans.rate.drop.threshold)
appDataStatistic.spanDropSumChartExplanation_4: Dropped due to consistent dropping: dropped because other spans of the same trace got dropped in the past , e.g. due to backpressure (ensure we drop all spans of a trace or none).
appDataStatistic.spanDropSumChartExplanation_5: Dropped due to backpressure: dropped because of resource exhaustion (e.g. high CPU usage or one step of the pipeline is a bottleneck).
appDataStatistic.spanDropSumChartExplanation_6: Dropped hard due to backpressure (random dropping): dropped because Kafka record is older than 5 seconds.
appDataStatistic.spanDropSumChartExplanation_7: Dropped due to trace throttler: dropped due to a rate limiter per trace (config.hard.spans.per.trace.rate.drop.threshold)
appDataStatistic.dropHardBackpressureRandom: Dropped hard due to backpressure (random dropping)
appDataStatistic.backendSpanDropInstChartExplanation_1: When spans are dropped, it is important to look at individual instances.
appDataStatistic.backendSpanDropInstChartExplanation_2: All of the instances are dropping: scale out.
appDataStatistic.backendSpanDropInstChartExplanation_3: One or several instances are dropping (but not all): scaling out will not help.
appDataStatistic.backendSpanDropInstChartExplanation_4: Traces with a high throughput are being processed (sharding key is the trace id): adjust config.hard.spans.per.trace.rate.drop.threshold.
appDataStatistic.backendSpanDropInstChartExplanation_5: CPU load is too high on the underlying host(s): assign instance to a less overloaded host.
appDataStatistic.spanLatencyMeanInstChartExplanation: Delay in the agent: delay between the time a span was ended and the time it was sent from the agent to acceptor.
appDataStatistic.acceptorRateLimitSpanhartExplan: Number of span messages (a message contains multiple spans) dropped due to a rate per-tenant-unit limiter. See config.span.publish.rate.limit (default: 25,000).

api.apiChartExplanation_1: API calls are blocked when they reached the rate limit as defined in the rateLimit config section of ui-backend.
api.apiChartExplanation_2: The HTTP status code 429 is given in the response, along the following headers (see <linkToDocs>reference</linkToDocs>):
api.apiChartExplanation_3: There is a default limit but also more specific ones per zone: search, settings, appdata, and snapshots.
api.apiChartExplanation_4: The below chart only tell you that calls are being blocked but we do not know which of the limits got reached. For that you can look at the com.instana.ui.resource.api.filter.ratelimit.RateLimitingFilter.distinct-client-key-ZONE metrics in ui-backend which give you the call rate per zone, or look closer at traces and more specifically status codes and headers.
api.apiChartExplanation_5: Important: Calls with HTTP status code 429 are not necessarily blocked by the API rate limiters, but can also be blocked by one of the limiters used to protect appdata-reader (see corresponding metrics in ui-backend with the format appDataReaderXXXLimiter). You can distinguish the 2 cases by looking at the presence of the X-RateLimit-XXX headers in the traces.
